item.title: Israel says killed two 'terrorists' working at MSF clinic
UN rapporteur warns Costa Rica will be held accountable over 'false' terrorism accusations
item.description:
The UN special rapporteur on Palestinian rights said Friday that Costa Rica will be held accountable for false "terrorism" accusations it leveled to deny her entry to the country.

Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide in Gaza and the occupied territories, spoke from the airport serving the capital city San Jose, after being denied entry as she arrived Thursday.

The US-aligned government of Costa Rica asserted that Albanese was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts."

item.title: US military fires on ship violating Iran blockade
US disables ship trying to leave Iran, as Tehran vows to confront blockade
item.description: DUBAI, Nov 27 (Reuters) - The US military said on Friday it disabled a commercial ship that attempted to run the US blockade of Iran, while an adviser to Iran's supreme leader said Tehran would keep the Strait of Hormuz shut and vowed to break the US embargo.

item.title: Costa Rica bars UN rapporteur on Palestinian territory, drawing concern from rights chief
item.description:
By Paolo Laudani and Alvaro Murillo

Nov 27 (Reuters) - Costa Rica denied entry to the United Nations special rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territory, drawing criticism from UN human rights chief Volker Turk on Friday.

Costa Rica's move put the small Central American country's increasingly close alignment with Washington and Israel on security and foreign policy into the spotlight.

item.description: A proposed expansion of South Korea's naval mission near the Strait of Hormuz has Tehran unsettled over prospects of a wider war and a potential loss of its leverage in the strategic waterway.

item.title: Tunisia NGO slams 'inhumane' prison conditions after dozens of detainee deaths
item.description:
Tunisia's main rights group on Friday denounced "inhumane" conditions in Tunisian prisons, saying 30 inmates have died since the beginning of summer, the country's hottest on record.

Authorities have yet to release figures for prison deaths after a summer marked by multiple heatwaves, water shortages and power cuts.

"The situation in prisons is inhumane and catastrophic," said Bassem Trifi, head of the Tunisian League for Human Rights, adding that "overcrowding and the lack of healthcare" in prisons were a major issue.

item.title: UN refugee agency seeks $7.1 bn in 2027
item.description:
The United Nations' refugee agency said on Friday it was seeking a much-reduced $7.1 billion to protect stateless people and respond to emergencies in 2027.

UNHCR chief Barham Salih warned last month that his agency was being "asked to do the impossible", over-stretched by a huge funding shortfall and near record-high population displacements around the world.

UNHCR's 2026 appeal targeted $8.5 billion -- of which only $2.9 billion has been raised to date.

item.title: War, fear drive Sudanese writer Baraka Sakin's fiction
item.description:
A lifetime of war and persecution has shaped the writing of Sudanese novelist Abdelaziz Baraka Sakin, who has turned the fear and longing that are so central to his experience into his main drive.

The 63-year-old fled Sudan for Europe in 2012 and then returned, dreaming of an end to his forced exile.

But the war that erupted in 2023 and killed more than 200,000 people pushed him out again.

Still, he keeps writing.

item.title: UN urges Costa Rica to let in Palestinians rapporteur
item.description:
The United Nations on Friday urged Costa Rica to urgently reconsider its ban on admitting the UN special rapporteur on Palestinian rights and let her into the country.

Costa Rica's government said Thursday it had denied entry to Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts".

Italian lawyer Albanese is the UN special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967.

item.title: Funding cuts force mass closures of shelters for refugee women, UN says
item.description:
By Emma Farge

GENEVA, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Nearly half of shelters for displaced women and girls across over a dozen countries have closed since the beginning of last year due to funding cuts, leaving them more vulnerable to sexual abuse and violence, the UN refugee agency said on Friday.

These safe spaces help survivors of war orabduction to seek psychological support and other services while protecting them from rape and abuse in camps where ill-lit, crowded conditions canincrease risks.

item.title: Trump backs Iraqi leader's efforts to assert more state authority
item.description:
Nov 27 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump on Friday backed the Iraqi leader's drive to assert state control, including stopping the smuggling of Iraqi oil, moves that put Baghdad in direct confrontation with Iran's militia allies and Kurdish authorities.

"We support Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s efforts to assert state authority throughout Iraq, stop the smuggling of Iraqi oil, end corruption, and bring all weapons under the exclusive control of the state," Trump said in a Truth Social post.

item.title: Turkey summons Georgia envoy over clashes at Besiktas match against Israeli club
item.description: Turkey called for a full investigation and legal action over what it described as “disproportionate” police force against the Turkish team’s fans during a match against Hapoel Beer-Sheva where 16 Turkish supporters were detained and later released.
